titulo: AGENTS.md, Skills, and memory you can check
lead: Every new conversation with the agent starts from zero. Without an instructions file, you repeat the same warnings; with a vague instruction, nothing changes. A rule you can check, a routine saved in a Skill, and a short dated memory make the agent get better with each task.
objetivo: rewrite AGENTS.md with five checkable rules and turn a real failure into a rule on the next run.
hero_alt: A hand pointing to an instruction sign posted on the door of a workroom.

aprende.t: Write an observable rule: action and evidence
Know which AGENTS.md applies: global, project, subfolder
Save a repeated procedure in a Skill
Dated memory and a failure with the smallest fix

secoes.titulo: A sign on the door, a routine in the file cabinet
secoes.sub: Where each type of instruction lives. Click each block.

nos.sub: The sign on the folder's door
nos.detalhe: It says how to work there: where to start reading, how to check, what not to do, and the format of the delivery. The history and the reasons stay out. A short file gets read in full.

nos.sub: The routine that comes out of the file cabinet
nos.detalhe: A procedure that repeats (the weekly list, the Friday report) becomes a Skill: a SKILL.md that starts with a name and a description. The agent triggers it when the task calls for it, without loading the whole manual on every task.

nos.sub: A bulletin board with a date and an owner
nos.detalhe: It's not the model learning: it's a file the agent reads when you point to it. Keep stable facts and decisions with a date and a reason, not the whole conversation. Mark the top with the date it was last reviewed.

Symptom, observed cause, smallest fix and check, all in one line. Say whether the failure came from the request or from the infrastructure. The fix goes where the next run reads it: the AGENTS.md or the Skill.

secoes.volta: A failure becomes a rule; the rule changes the next task
secoes.legenda: None of these files overrides the system instructions, the tool's permissions, or what you explicitly ask for in the conversation.

rolagem_fim.texto: A rule you can check at the door, a script in the file cabinet, short dated memory, and every slip turning into a small safeguard. That's how tomorrow's task comes out better than today's, without switching models.

texto: Try the sign test: "wear safety glasses" can be checked by looking; "be careful" can't.
A good rule asks for one action and leaves evidence in the delivery. A rule that doesn't change any decision gets removed from the file.

exemplo.texto: Compare the report total with vendas.csv and state the difference.

texto: In Codex, the global AGENTS.md lives in %USERPROFILE%\.codex and applies everywhere; the project one applies in its folder; the one in a subfolder takes precedence inside it.
Strange behavior? Look for a forgotten AGENTS.override.md in a copied folder: in the same folder, it takes priority over AGENTS.md.

exemplo.texto: Summarize the instructions you loaded and say which file each one came from.

passos.sub: The description says when to use it and when not to
texto: The description is what the agent reads to decide whether to trigger the Skill. "Helps with reports" fires even on meeting minutes.
State the situation and where it stops. Before you trust it, rehearse with three cases: normal, incomplete and outside what was agreed.

exemplo.texto: Generate a weekly report draft when there is a sales CSV. Do not use it to send reports or handle credentials.

texto: When the result comes out wrong, the urge is to switch models or redo everything. That burns hours and hides a simple problem.
A request failure is fixed in the text; an infrastructure failure, with a check. One new line in AGENTS.md is usually enough.

exemplo.texto: Check the header and the number of records before generating.

secoes.sub: Copy and adapt to your folder. Replace whatever is between < >.

blocos.conteudo:
# Instructions for the agent

Purpose: <what this project produces>

1. Read README.md before changing anything.
2. Use only entradas/ and saidas/; do not delete or rename files.
3. Do not invent data that is not in the inputs; anything missing becomes a pending item at the end.
4. Never write keys or passwords in a text file; cite only the name of the variable from .env.
5. Finish by saying: what you changed, how you checked it and what remains pending.

---
name: relatorio-semanal
description: Generate a weekly report draft when the user provides a sales CSV. Do not use it to send reports or handle credentials.
---

## Input
A CSV in entradas/.

## Steps
1. Check the header and the number of records before generating.
2. Add up the values; do not invent missing ones.
3. Write the draft to saidas/relatorio.md.

## Output and check
Cite the source, the known total and the pending items. Stop before sending or publishing.

# Memory
Reviewed on: <dd/mm/yyyy>

- <stable fact 1, e.g.: short reports, pending items at the end>
- <stable fact 2>
- <stable fact 3>

| Date | Symptom | Observed cause | Smallest fix | Check | Type |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| <dd/mm> | empty report | spreadsheet with no records | check the number of rows before generating | an empty spreadsheet gives a warning, not a report | infrastructure |
Summarize the instructions you loaded in this folder and say which file each one came from. Then, consult ../config/memoria.md and, when you do the next task, say which fact from the memory you used.

blocos.rot: cmd · create the Skill folder and check it

abas.html:
• "Be excellent." → how to check: there is no way.
  • "Compare the total with vendas.csv and state the difference." → the deliverable includes the sum and the difference.
  • "Review everything very carefully." → replace it with "List the open items at the end".

1. %USERPROFILE%\.codex\AGENTS.md: global, small ("report what you checked").
  2. projetos\meu-primeiro-agente\AGENTS.md: applies in the project.
  3. …\provas\AGENTS.md: takes precedence inside provas for what it covers.

Your explicit request in the conversation outweighs all three.

Without the "don't invent missing values" rule: "Week total: 100.00" — the Pen had no value and the total pretended it did.

With the rule: "Known total: 90.50. Open item: the Pen row has no value. I did not fill it in."

exercicios.titulo: E13 · Five rules you can check
exercicios.texto: Rewrite AGENTS.md with five rules. Next to each one, note how you check whether it was followed. Ask for a task and check.
exercicios.pronto: for each of the five rules, you point to the evidence in the agent's deliverable that it was followed.

exercicios.titulo: E14 · The failure becomes a rule
exercicios.texto: Record a real failure from the earlier lessons in config\falhas.md (symptom, cause, smallest fix, check, type) and put the fix in AGENTS.md.
exercicios.pronto: on the next task, the same problem does not repeat and you can say which line of AGENTS.md prevented it.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: Which of these rules can you check by looking at the agent's deliverable?
opcoes: List the open items at the end.
perguntas.explica: An observable rule has an action and evidence: the list of open items is either at the end or it isn't. The others leave no trace.

perguntas.p: The global file says "answer in bullet points," the project's AGENTS.md says nothing about format, and you ask for a table in the conversation. Which one wins?
opcoes: The table requested in the conversation.
perguntas.explica: The explicit request in the conversation outweighs the instruction files.

perguntas.p: You created memoria.md in config, but the agent ignored the facts. What do you do first?
opcoes: Point to the file in the request itself and ask for the fact it used.
Copy more conversations into the file.
perguntas.explica: The file existing does not guarantee it gets read. Say which file to consult and ask the agent to cite the fact it used.

perguntas.p: The report came out empty because the spreadsheet had no records. What is the smallest fix?
opcoes: One rule: check the number of records before generating.
perguntas.explica: An infrastructure failure is fixed with a small check. Rebuilding takes hours and the empty spreadsheet keeps breaking things.
